newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy metalworker union "optimistic" on talks.
newsitem.headline: Italy metalworker union "optimistic" on talks.

text.p: A leader of an Italian metalworkers' union said he was "optimistic" following all-night talks with employers and a new government proposal to end a pay dispute.
"The board of UILM will evaluate the merits of the government proposoal tomorrow and will give a final opinion. I am optimistic," UILM leader Luiti Angeletti said.
UILM together with the FIM and FIOM unions represent Italy's metal workers and engineers who have been involved in a pay dispute with employers since their contract expired last June.
Prime Minister Romano Prodi convened a round of all-night talks ending at 0700 GMT on Monday after which the government forwarded its newest proposal to end the dispute.

Union leaders have said they expected to give their response to the proposal later on Monday or Tuesday, and that a new meeting between the unions and employers' group Federmeccanica was likely to take place on Tuesday at the Labour Ministry.
